audit.title: Create a Time-Based Upkeep

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with a task-scoped H1 and "This guide explains how to register time-based upkeeps," but leads with marketing ("Create powerful automation") rather than a self-contained definition. Sections are step-titled, so most lift cleanly, but the top chunk doesn't answer "what is a time-based upkeep."

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. 8 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips, median 65 words/section (measured). Well-suited to RAG chunking; only gap is the absence of a table for gas requirements.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Decent in spots — "roughly 110K gas per call," "add 150K additional gas," CRON field ranges, list max length 26. But measured prose has only 4 numerals (7/1k words) and 0 with units; most specifics live in the code block. Room to surface numbers into prose.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Good — 13 links, 2 to primary sources (docs.soliditylang.org, github.com pinned to a commit). One opaque link ("please see") should get descriptive anchor text.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Weak. No crisp one-sentence definition of "time-based upkeep," "CronUpkeep," or "Job Scheduler" near first use. Engines have nothing verbatim-liftable to define the concept.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags, head not captured. This is the weakest dimension and a site-level pattern; no `TechArticle` schema or visible freshness signal for agents to trust.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: The single fenced block is the CRON format reference and is untagged (measured: 1 untagged, languages [none]). It's explanatory, not runnable, which is acceptable for a UI-driven guide, but it should be language-tagged and a sample valid CRON string shown.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers setup → register → monitor, but has no troubleshooting/FAQ and no symptom-phrased sections (e.g. "upkeep not executing on schedule," "invalid CRON expression"). Misses the error-string queries devs actually type.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean and consistent ("upkeep," "CronUpkeep," "Automation app" used uniformly). Minor marketing fluff at the top; otherwise unambiguous.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-chunked procedural guide for registering time-based (CRON) upkeeps through the Chainlink Automation app. Its biggest strength is structure — short, coherent sections with no level skips and useful inline links to primary sources (Solidity ABI spec, the `CronUpkeepFactory` source). Its biggest opportunity is discoverability and definition: the page carries no JSON-LD/canonical/date metadata, never crisply defines "time-based upkeep" in a liftable sentence, and lacks any symptom- or question-phrased headings that match how devs actually query. The headline verdict: content is solid but under-instrumented for retrieval — it will be missed or under-cited on the intent queries it should own.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased sections for the debug lifecycle
recommendations.where: new H2s near the end, after "Complete upkeep registration"
recommendations.issue: No troubleshooting; monitoring is one sentence: "You must monitor the balance of your upkeep."
recommendations.change: Add "Why is my time-based upkeep not executing?" and "What CRON expressions are supported?" sections answering with the underfunded/minimum-balance case and the CRON limitations (no `? L W #`, no year field, UTC-only, list max 26).
recommendations.why: Devs query by symptom, not concept title; question headings win retrieval that step-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add a liftable canonical definition up top
recommendations.where: first paragraph, replacing "Create powerful automation for your smart contract…"
recommendations.issue: Opens with marketing, not a definition.
recommendations.change: Lead with: "A time-based upkeep executes a chosen function on your smart contract on a fixed CRON schedule, without requiring you to write an Automation-compatible contract. Chainlink deploys a `CronUpkeep` contract to run the schedule."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a self-contained, verbatim-liftable answer to "what is a time-based upkeep."

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no date signals.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified`, canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) and parseability; note head could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm.

recommendations.title: Surface the gas math into a small table
recommendations.issue: Gas guidance is buried in a NOTE callout prose.
recommendations.change: Add a 2-row table: `CronUpkeep overhead ≈ 110K gas/call` / `Recommended buffer +150K gas`, plus "must not exceed `performGasLimit`."
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract quantitative reasons and lift them into justified answers.

recommendations.title: Tag the code fence and show a concrete CRON example
recommendations.change: Tag it (e.g. ```` ```text ````) and add a labeled runnable example: `*/5 * * * *` → "runs every 5 minutes (UTC)."
recommendations.why: Labeled, self-contained snippets are more reliably parsed and quoted by agents.

recommendations.title: Give the opaque link descriptive anchor text
recommendations.where: "If you want to use dynamic inputs please see [Custom logic Upkeeps]"
recommendations.issue: Measured: 1 opaque link; and "(Image: Image)" placeholders provide no alt context.
recommendations.change: Ensure anchor text names the target; add descriptive alt text to the screenshot placeholders.
recommendations.why: Descriptive anchors and alt text aid entity resolution and link-context extraction.

antiPatterns: Mild marketing fluff in the opening sentence ("Create powerful automation").
Repeated non-descriptive image placeholders ("(Image: Image)") — no alt text for agents.
Missing date/freshness signal (measured: no dateModified) — undated content.
offPageNotes: Metadata gaps (JSON-LD, canonical, og/twitter, dates) are almost certainly a **site-level template** issue — fix once in the docs framework to lift every page.
The page already references `/llms.txt`; ensure this guide is indexed there under both its concept name and symptom phrasings.
Head metadata could not be captured in this run — pass raw `<head>` to the CLI for a definitive metadata read.
